record.paper_title: Infrared tip-tilt sensing: on-sky experience, lessons learned and unsolved problems
record.original_question: How can an infrared tip-tilt sensor accurately measure image displacement for faint, extended astronomical sources, rather than point-like guide stars, when conventional centroiding algorithms are not well suited to extended-object structure?

evidence.quote: A related issue is optimal tip-tilt sensing with extended objects, for which conventional centroiding algorithms are not well suited.
There are still a number of unsolved research problems and these are listed here: – Measuring centroids from faint, extended sources.

artifact.category_tag: Centroiding of extended sources in adaptive optics
artifact.status_search_result: Centroiding of faint, extended sources for tip-tilt sensing is widely discussed in the adaptive-optics literature as an unresolved practical and theoretical issue. No standard, provably optimal real-time algorithm has been established; recent work proposes correlation-based and machine-learning approaches but none is recognized as a complete solution.
